notes: The 23-day placebo gave shootings 1.008 (0.969 to 1.048), ambulance incidents 0.998 (0.992 to 1.003) and injury crashes 1.002 (0.988 to 1.016), so the full-moon estimates are no different from a window with no meaning. The graph's 1.042 for crash transports in Japan (PMID 29990928) is for full-moon nights. Spread over three whole days it would be about 1.004, which the injury-crash interval does not exclude, so the two do not conflict. The graph's homicide finding for Finland (0.85, PMID 30647032) is outside the shooting interval. Secondary, deciding nothing: the full-moon day alone gave shootings 1.033 (0.957 to 1.114) and injury crashes 0.980 (0.957 to 1.003). Referee, 14 November: the numbers reproduce and stay inside the bounds under quasi-Poisson and negative-binomial errors and 5- and 7-day windows. Rule 11 read literally would give unsettled, since the placebo also meets support_if; rule 13 records how rule 11 applies to a prediction of no effect. Exploratory and unexplained: a 3-day window centred 4 days before the full moon gives 0.914 for shootings (z = -3.9), in both decades; it is outside the registered window and decides nothing.
